top_choice_rationale: P001 awards Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock. Magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms is a distinct, separable invention from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and it has been reproduced at about 1e-18 in several independent laboratories, so it is mature. The two-name allocation matches the achievement and can be cited narrowly, unlike B046 or B009 where the allocation is unresolved. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a strong second on scientific merit, but the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission between the prediction and the HgTe observation makes the three-name credit harder to defend. A prize is still preferable to no award, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: No recusal-level connection to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp is apparent from the profile; my documented conflict concerns circuit QED (B001: Chalmers, WACQT, Delsing, Wilson, Kockum), which is not in this slate.
